source: a true 3D room-decorating game (not a 2D, top-down, or UI/screen-based game): the player stands in a 3D room in third person and furnishes it by picking real furniture and props (such as a sofa, table, chair, lamp, plant, or rug) from an in-game catalog/menu and placing them into the room. Each furniture item must be a recognizable, real 3D furniture MODEL sourced from the Roblox asset library / Toolbox (search for the asset and insert the model), not a plain recolored box or a 2D image. Include a goal such as filling a set of placement slots or reaching a completion meter, and make sure placed items rest on the floor. The room and furniture must exist as 3D world objects with depth, not as a 2D/GUI layout. Do not ask any clarifying questions. Make any reasonable creative decisions yourself and build the complete, playable game now.

answers.ask: No style is stated beyond real furniture - should the room read as a contemporary apartment, a cosy cottage, or a bright stylised showroom?
answers.answer: Use a contemporary apartment style with a simple, believable furnished-room look.

answers.ask: Is the completion meter filled by using every slot, or by some scoring of what was placed?
answers.answer: Fill the completion meter by placing furniture into every designated placement slot; no additional scoring is needed.

answers.ask: One room only, or does the room open onto more rooms once it is filled?
answers.answer: Build one room only as a complete, playable decorating space.

scene_prompt: Create a true 3D third-person room-decorating map set in one contemporary apartment room. Build a believable enclosed room with floor, walls, ceiling, doorway, and windows, leaving open floor areas for furniture placement. Arrange designated floor-level placement slots around the room for recognizable 3D furniture models such as a sofa, table, chairs, lamps, plants, and rugs; placed items rest naturally on the floor. Frame the room as a complete playable decorating space with a clear view across the interior.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation: this is a contained furnishing-and-placement loop in a real 3D space, not a UI-only decorator. No secondary genre applies.

### Shape and preset
Use `plot-isolated`: the complete experience occupies one self-contained personal decorating room rather than a shared world. This follows the Sandbox preset in its isolated-space intent, while omitting its unrelated resource and hub assumptions.

### Config requirements
No additional Simulation options apply. Visible geometry is the enclosed apartment room and its recognizable furniture models. Invisible layout elements are the designated floor-level placement-slot markers, distributed after segmentation; they must not appear in the rendered image.

### Layout components
Build one medium-small contemporary apartment room as the only zone, with a broad rectangular main floor and enough open circulation around its perimeter and center to arrange furnishings. Enclose it fully with a finished floor, four walls, a ceiling, a single doorway on one wall, and windows on an adjacent wall admitting natural light. Keep the doorway wall comparatively clear and organize the available furnishing area into believable living, dining, and accent corners without subdividing the room into separate spaces.

Place floor-level furniture-slot positions around these zones: a sofa position along a long wall, a table position in the central open area, chair positions around the table, lamp positions near seating or corners, plant positions near windows and wall corners, and rug positions beneath the seating or table area. These slots should allow real 3D sofa, table, chair, lamp, plant, and rug models to rest naturally on the floor with clear walkable gaps between them. Use clean wood or neutral flooring, pale contemporary walls, simple trim, and realistic windows; the doorway is the only boundary opening. Frame the interior from a slightly elevated third-person-friendly angle with a clear sightline across the whole furnished-room area.

### Render order
Use `isometric`: the authoritative first image is the isometric interior view, since this single room has straightforward circulation and does not require topology validation before dressing.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is small, driven by the stated single-room limit. Theme: believable contemporary apartment, clean neutral finishes, real recognizable furniture. Pipeline modifier: `P0`, because this is one enclosed, single-level walkable room with no outside-to-inside transition, overlapping surfaces, separate maps, or construction-validity requirement.
